key_insight: The paper proposes ecological foundation models that combine diverse ecological data with ecological theory. The goal is to make predictions that generalize better across ecosystems and scales.
problem_solved: Ecological data and theories are fragmented across sources, scales and approaches, making it difficult to develop broadly applicable predictions.
method: Bring large, multimodal ecological datasets into a shared modeling framework.
Incorporate ecological theory alongside data-driven learning.
Aim for predictions that transfer across ecological settings; the provided abstract does not report implementation details or validation results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this proposal highlights a path toward domain-grounded foundation models rather than relying on data scale alone. It emphasizes generalization across heterogeneous scientific data and settings.
visual_elements: Converging streams of ecological data and theory feeding a foundation model.
A scale ladder connecting organisms, communities and ecosystems.
A transfer diagram showing one model applied across different habitats.
A contrast between fragmented datasets and an integrated modeling framework.
paper_authors: Ross J. Gardiner, Henry Cerbone, Hammed A. Akande, Carly H. Batist, Amber Cowans
